text: True or False: A trained deep-learning surrogate model is always cheaper than the electromagnetic solver it replaces, so it pays off for any design task.
explanation: False — a surrogate only pays off once it is queried more than its own training cost of roughly 10^3 to 10^5 simulations, so it wins only when the base simulation is expensive and the design space is scanned many times. For a one-off device, running the solver or adjoint optimization directly is cheaper; deep learning caches physics, it does not create it for free.
